page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What ZSM-5 is
lines: ZSM-5 is a zeolite, that is a hydrated
It is made in the laboratory, not mined.
It is used as a catalyst.
steps.why: A zeolite framework is porous, so a reacting molecule can enter a cavity, where the framework surrounds it on every side. That is what allows a solid aluminosilicate such as ZSM-5 to act as a catalyst.
common_mistakes: Calling ZSM-5 a mineral of no fixed structure. It is a zeolite made in the laboratory, an aluminosilicate with cavities of a definite size.
Writing that ZSM-5 is a reactant. It is a catalyst and is not used up.
steps.memory_tip: ZSM-5 is a zeolite, and a zeolite is a hydrated aluminosilicate with cavities.
steps.margin_note: Name it as a zeolite before giving the use, so the use has something to stand on.

steps.label: The use
lines: The alcohol is passed over the heated
catalyst and comes off as the mixture
The word directly is part of the
answer: no separate stage is needed in
steps.why: The cavities of ZSM-5 are of about the size of the hydrocarbon molecules that make up gasoline, so the products that form inside them are of that size. That is why the product comes off as gasoline-sized molecules rather than as a wide mixture.
common_mistakes: Writing that ZSM-5 is used only to soften hard water. Softening water is a use of zeolites in general; the use asked for here is the conversion of alcohols into gasoline.
Naming petrol from crude oil. ZSM-5 converts alcohols, not crude oil.
steps.memory_tip: ZSM-5 takes an alcohol in and gives gasoline out, in one step.
steps.margin_note: One line naming the alcohol as the starting material and gasoline as the product completes the answer.
